newsitem.title: HUNGARY: OSCE urges Slovakia to pass minority language law.
newsitem.headline: OSCE urges Slovakia to pass minority language law.

text.p: The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) on Monday urged Slovakia to pass a minority language law, long-awaited by ethnic Hungarians in Slovakia.

"As I know, the Slovak constitution contains a clause which requires a law about the language use of ethnic minorities in official contacts," Max van der Stoel, OSCE high commissioner on national minorities told the Hungarian news agency MTI.
"I hope this law is being prepared," he added.
Stoel spoke with MTI following his talks with Hungarian Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs.
Earlier this month, Kovacs appealed to Slovakia to pass the law, saying Bratislava was contravening its international commitments to its ethnic Hungarian minority by delaying the legislation.
The law is a requirement of the basic treaty ratified by Hungary and Slovakia last year which guarantees current borders, human rights, and the protection of minorities.

The Slovak government, led by Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar, provoked international condemenation by introducing a controversial language law late in 1995 making Slovak the only language to be used in public places.
However, it also promised to pass a law protecting minority languages but has so far failed to put the bill before parliament.
